source: User clarification 2026-10-30: CPU improvements and GPU improvements jointly count; overall CPU-GPU faster than original VPR is the primary goal.
primary_goal: Quality-qualified end-to-end CPU-GPU workflow improvement over explicitly configured original VPR.
acceptable_result: T_joint < T_original; incremental GPU gain over improved CPU is desirable, not a prerequisite for joint improvement.
attribution: Measure improved CPU and original multithreaded controls to explain benefits and select the best configuration; do not use missing GPU-only attribution to dismiss joint benefits.

existing_gemm_observation.scope: single diagnostic run, not production confirmation

next_steps: First confirm GEMM joint end-to-end behavior without diagnostic events/capture/replay, using repeated same-worker original and joint runs with fixed inputs and explicit thread counts.
Include original four-CPU and improved CPU/guard controls as attribution and configuration evidence; a GPU-only incremental win is not the joint-success gate.
Optimize CPU scheduling, partition/task publication, data handling and lookahead as well as GPU search, prioritized by whole-process cost.
Resolve elliptic convergence and verify quality before reporting speedup.
